name: application-budget-progress-bar
title: Budget Progress Bar
description: Spend-vs-budget progress bar that turns red and shows an explicit overspend amount when spending exceeds budget — fill width and over-budget state are both computed from real numbers.
useWhen: Tracking spend against a fixed budget where exceeding it is a meaningful, visually distinct state.
You want the bar to cap at 100% width and show an explicit overspend label instead of clipping or overflowing silently.
The amounts should be real currency figures, not generic percentages.
avoidWhen: There's no hard budget ceiling — a plain progress-bars component is simpler for open-ended progress.
You're tracking a resource quota (API calls, storage) rather than money — use usage-meter-card instead.
You need multiple budget categories compared at once — use segment-breakdown-bar or a table instead.
responsiveBehavior: The bar and label are a fluid-width block that scales with its container at any width.
accessibility: The filled bar carries role='img' with an aria-label stating spent amount, budget, and the overspend amount when over budget.
Over-budget state is conveyed by both bar/text color and an explicit "$X over budget" text line, not color alone.
The bar visually caps at 100% width even when overspending, avoiding a bar that breaks out of its container.

variants.title: Budget progress bar
variants.description: Marketing budget over its $5,000 limit at $5,420 spent, showing the red over-budget state and a $420 overspend label, on a light surface.
accessibility: Overspend amount is computed as spent minus budget, so it can never drift out of sync with the displayed figures.

variants.title: Budget progress bar (Dark)
variants.description: The same over-budget marketing spend example, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Bar and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
